correctness.rationale: For n≥9, maximal open-neighborhood simplices are Q_i={i±1,i±2}. Unique common-neighbor intersections make n pairs (B_i,Q_i) and n further edge-triangle pairs (E_i,C_i) free; the remaining invariant 2-complex has (V,E,F)=(n,3n,2n), connected 6-cycle vertex links and a primitive integral 2-cycle, hence is a torus. Reflections preserve its orientation; signed fixed simplices give Lefschetz L=4 on every reflection, while nonidentity rotations give L=0. Rank-two finite-order matrices must be -I and I respectively, and finite-group averaging yields rational quotient cohomology of S². The inspected verify.py checks n=9..80, but the proof is uniform via intersections and surface topology.
